questions.explain: Risk is not a property of the diff alone — altering a table that serves 40% of batch requests is far riskier than altering a cold object.
options: The number of lines in the migration script
The intersection of the schema diff with production workload via Query Store hot-object overlap
The time of day the pipeline runs
The seniority of the developer who wrote the change
questions.q: What is the most important feature for deployment risk scoring, according to the chapter?

questions.explain: The pipeline proves the script (parse scan, clone dry-run, idempotency check) and the human approves the proven artifact — never generate-and-apply.
options: Generate the script and apply it immediately to save time
Skip verification for low-risk scripts
Let the model approve its own blast radius
Generate, then verify via automated checks, then human review — the model proposes, the pipeline proves, the DBA approves
questions.q: What is the correct lifecycle for an AI-generated migration script?

questions.explain: Deterministic rules catch the obvious cases (any sysadmin grant is security-relevant); the model handles the ambiguous middle, consulting index usage stats.
options: Deterministic rules for obvious cases plus model judgment for ambiguous ones, informed by sys.dm_db_index_usage_stats
A single LLM call with no rules
Manual review of every diff line
Ignoring cosmetic drift entirely
questions.q: How should drift severity classification combine rules and models?

questions.explain: Scoping to changed objects keeps unrelated workload noise out; triage classifies deltas as regression, expected change, or noise.
options: Watch all queries on the instance equally
Disable Query Store during the window
Scope the Query Store regression watch to changed objects and triage deltas as regression, expected change, or noise
Roll back automatically on any delta
questions.q: How does post-deploy verification avoid drowning in unrelated workload noise?

questions.explain: Every deploy outcome — clean, rolled back, incident — becomes labeled training data that makes the next risk score smarter.
options: Deploy history is only useful for compliance audits
Every deploy outcome feeds the labeled dataset that trains the next risk model, closing the intelligence loop
Risk models are trained once and never updated
Post-deploy data is discarded after 24 hours
questions.q: Why does the chapter emphasize logging every deploy outcome into a history dataset?
